text:
Jacek Karpiński was born on April 9, 1927, in Turin, Italy, to Polish intellectuals and alpinists. His father was an aeronautic engineer and inventor, and his mother was a physician. He was involved in the Polish resistance effort during World War II, severely injuring himself in 1943 while working on homemade bombs. He participated in the Warsaw Uprising and sustained a gunshot wound to the backbone, resulting in paralysis, for which he was awarded the Cross of Valour three times.
Post-war, Karpiński studied at Warsaw University of Technology, graduating in 1951. He worked on various projects, including the Analytical Analyzer of Harmonics (AAH) in 1957. His major contribution was the construction of AKAT-1 in 1959, which was the world's first differential equations analyzer based on transistors. Following his UNESCO scholarship in the United States, he implemented a Polish perceptron in 1964. Later, he designed the KAR-65, a mathematical machine, and established his own institution to develop K-202, an innovative minicomputer in 1970, though it ultimately did not reach mass production.
